recap.text: Theia is a goddess who stores worshippers as balls of light in a pocket until they party at her temple. The Pacifist network sponsors her to protect Crawler Carl because she is Samantha's mother. Samantha finds her mother is a boy eagle, a form driven by an agent named Rectrix. Carl is named friend of the church at Theia's temple, placing her on a list between Nekhebit and Yemaya.
Samantha tells a recap of her plan to greet or kill her mother, Theia. A skyfowl dude tells her that Theia is not really her mother. Samantha calls him a weirdo before the club goes nuts.

beats.headline: A party in her pocket
beats.text: Rosetta's briefing on how a warlord disappears. One of two immortals can carry her to a temple; the goddess is named Theia. Her prospective worshippers become balls of light that fit in an adherent's pocket, and at her temple they are released and spend several weeks being wooed and partying. It is a loophole: step away from the war and enjoy the rest of it. Theia is not a goddess clerics use, so no crawler ever stumbles into her temple. A perfect hiding place.
beats.gist: Theia is a goddess who hides warlords as balls of light in an adherent's pocket.

beats.headline: Sponsored, for once
beats.text: Theia has a long history with the Ascendency and is a poor bet for the throne, so nobody ever sponsors her. This season someone did, in the employ of the Pacifist network, not Porthus. They bought her to protect Crawler Carl, because she is Samantha's mother. She was the god who appeared at the end of the fifth floor to kill Slit, when in theory she was enraged at Samantha. Rosetta believes Vinata usually picks her. If Vinata did this season, Theia would smite her court.
beats.gist: The Pacifist network sponsors Theia, Samantha's mother, to protect Crawler Carl.

beats.headline: A boy eagle behind the altar
beats.text: The backup plan: Samantha was promised a way into her mother's temple, in the hope that Theia's clerics would help. She came out shouting. Her mother was an eagle, a boy eagle. A sponsored god may appear in its own form, and whoever drives Theia is a male skyfowl. Baroness Victory walks in and Samantha accuses her of momnapping. Victory's reply is procedural: sponsors making deities act outside their nature is cheating, and she has reminded both the Maestro and someone named Rectrix.
beats.gist: Samantha promised a way into Theia's temple, but found a male skyfowl behind the altar.

beats.headline: Friend of the church
beats.text: An achievement bans Crawler Carl from Club Vanquisher and from every temple, except his own god's and those that have named him friend of the church. Theia's is on that list, between Nekhebit and Yemaya. Carl works through the list for surprises. Theia is not one of them: the Open Intellect's agent, Rectrix, is driving her.
beats.gist: An achievement bans Carl from temples, but Theia's temple names him friend of the church.

beats.headline: Not really your mother
beats.text: Samantha's recap of the previous floor, delivered at speed. Her plan was to say hi to, and possibly kill, her own mother, whose name is Theia. When she got there it was some skyfowl dude, who said, "Look, I'm not really your mother," and then clarified: Theia isn't. Samantha's reply, as she tells it: "Yeah, okay, weirdo." Then the club went nuts, and her recap moves on to the next item.
beats.gist: Samantha tells how a skyfowl dude says Theia is not really her mother.

relations.note: Vinata's court usually hides in her temple
